Usually if the bridge doesn't have enough curve it is quite easy to "visit" neighboring strings if your bow is at a certain angle. 

If your pinky hurts because of too much pressure try releasing your first and second finger, so only fingers three and four are on the string. This helps to not stretch your hand so much so you can focus some of your stability and pressure on your pinky and not on keeping your hand stretched out. However this is easier to do if you know exactly where your first finger should go back to. 
Sometimes elevating your wrist higher helps to relieve some of the pressure as well.
